why: Doc sentence verified verbatim (curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new/2026-w29.md, line 63; it is a one-clause <div> in the digest-wins-grid, no second half that reverses it). The cited spawner lines are also accurate as far as they go: packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:110 is `export const DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH = 1`, :518-519 is the `Subagent depth limit exceeded` return, and `grep -ra -F` for MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION / MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS over packages/ apps/ really is 0 hits. But the CONSEQUENCE is false, and it is false exactly in the recurring shape this repo's trap list names: the enforcement lives one layer up, in the host, not in the spawner. (1) A per-session spawn COUNT budget DOES exist. spawner.ts:600-608 forwards `budgets: { fanout: cfg.maxFanout ?? 100, concurrency: cfg.concurrency ?? DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY, ... }` to the host, and packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.ts:148 enforces it inside the persisted-state commit: `if (children.length >= input.budgets.fanout) throw new Error('child-session-fanout-limit')`. `children` is the parent session's FULL child-record list; records are removed only on the cancelled-start rollback (:154), never on completion, so `children.length` is a CUMULATIVE per-session spawn count, not an active count. child-session-service.test.ts:178-184 proves the cumulative semantics: child-1 is stopped first, and a subsequent start with `fanout: 1` still throws `child-session-fanout-limit`. The value comes from `orchestrator.maxAgents` (pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1280 `maxFanout: config.orchestrator?.maxAgents`), default 1000 in DEFAULT_PI_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:109); the spawner's own fallback when the host supplies nothing is 100. (2) A concurrency limit DOES exist, in BOTH layers. spawner.ts:144-208 defines a `Semaphore` sized by `computeEffectiveConcurrency(cfg.concurrency ?? 16)` = `max(1, min(ceiling, cpuCores - 2))`, rebuilt on every `configureSpawner` (:208), and every spawn goes through `semaphore.run(...)`. The host re-checks independently at child-session-service.ts:149: `if (active.length >= input.budgets.concurrency) throw new Error('child-session-concurrency-limit')`. Both are covered by tests (spawner.test.ts imports `computeEffectiveConcurrency`/`Semaphore`; child-session-service.test.ts:172 and :370 assert `child-session-concurrency-limit`). (3) 'A depth-1 loop can spawn unboundedly' is therefore false on two counts: the Nth spawn of a session is refused once N reaches the fanout budget, and at most min(16, cores-2) run at once meanwhile. Budgets are additionally clamped monotonically down the tree (SessionManager.ts:11142-11143 `Math.min(input.budgets.fanout, inherited.fanout)` / same for concurrency, and :4933-4934 pins a child's fanout/concurrency to 1), and the workflow tool carries its own per-run cap (workflow-tool.ts:562-563, `workflow maxAgents exceeded`). This is not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (those are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions) and it is not a subscription/brand product difference; it is simply a wrong consequence drawn from a true identifier absence. What actually survives is a naming/default difference, not a missing mechanism.
correctedState: A session-wide subagent spawn cap and a concurrency cap both exist; only the Claude env-var names do not. Enforcement is in the host, not the spawner: packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.ts:148 refuses a start with 'child-session-fanout-limit' once the parent session's cumulative child-record count reaches budgets.fanout (records are pruned only on cancelled-start rollback at :154, so the count is cumulative for the session — proven by child-session-service.test.ts:178-184, where a stopped child still counts), and :149 refuses with 'child-session-concurrency-limit' once active children reach budgets.concurrency. The spawner supplies those budgets at spawner.ts:600-608 (fanout = cfg.maxFanout ?? 100, concurrency = cfg.concurrency ?? 16) and independently gates every spawn through a Semaphore sized max(1, min(concurrency, cpuCores - 2)) (spawner.ts:136-142, :204-208, :592). The fanout ceiling is configured as orchestrator.maxAgents, default 1000 (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:109), wired at packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1280. Budgets clamp monotonically down the tree (SessionManager.ts:11142-11143, :4933-4934). The real divergence is therefore narrow: our cap is a config key (orchestrator.maxAgents / orchestrator.concurrency on the execution manifest) rather than the CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION env var, and the default is 1000 (100 when the host supplies nothing) rather than Claude's 200 — not an absent limit, and not an unbounded depth-1 loop.
